Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our security team:  

- PII scope: patient names, DOB, MRN, and clinician notes. We will flag which pipelines process PHI; at least two pipelines must be air-gapped.
- Retention: default retention for stored logs should be no more than 30 days; for compliance reasons we may want option to set to 90 days for audit windows. Can Redwood support configurable retention per environment?

- Egress: can Redwood guarantee zero egress to the public internet from the inference nodes when deployed in our VPC? If not, we need details on destinations and ports.

Hi all,

Thanks for the details, Bob. Short answers first: yes, most of this is supported; a few notes and configuration options below.

1) VPC / zero egress
- If we deploy Redwood Private inside your VPC (customer-hosted control plane or private subnet), inference nodes do not require outbound access to the public internet for model serving. All network traffic can be kept inside the VPC and routed to your managed endpoints (e.g., S3, KMS) via VPC endpoints (no NAT required).
- We can provide a list of required ports/IP ranges for optional control-plane telemetry if you opt-in; otherwise control-plane calls can be routed over a private peering link or disabled for strict air-gapped installs.

2) On-prem / air-gapped pipelines
- For fully air-gapped workloads, we offer an on-prem package that runs the inference runtime and orchestration entirely within customer network boundaries. This requires an installation window and our PS team for model artifact staging. No external egress is required once artifacts are staged.
- Note: certain enterprise features (automatic model updates, remote support) are opt-in; disabling those increases maintenance overhead on your side.

3) PII / request/response persistence
- We support disabling request/response persistence for named environments. When disabled, transient inference requests are served in-memory and not written to Redwood-managed logs or storage.
- For additional safety, we provide per-route redaction hooks that can strip or hash specific fields before logs are emitted.

4) Logging & retention
- Audit metadata (timestamps, request ids, model/version, route) can be exported to your S3 bucket and encrypted with your KMS. We can configure lifecycle policies (30/90/365 days) on the exported logs to meet retention requirements.
- Customer can also run a log-forwarder inside the VPC to collect and retain logs entirely under their control.

5) Compliance artifacts (SOC2)
- Attaching a SOC2 excerpt and a short ops note on the private deployment process (SOC2-extract.pdf). This should help procurement.

Next steps I recommend:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) focused on the two air-gapped pipelines and artifact staging process.
- Provide sample network ACL/SG template + ports we need to open (I’ll attach redwood-private-network-ops.pdf).

If you want, I can join 6/24 at 10am PT for the deep-dive.

—Rishi
